title: Find vectorized code, then write an SSE2 loop
brief: Write a C array-add loop, detect packed vector instructions in clang's output at -O0, -O2, and -O3 -mavx2, then write the loop yourself in SSE2 assembly, four int32 at a time.
hints: add_arrays_c: `void add_arrays(int *dst, const int *a, const int *b, long n)` with a plain for loop over a long index. The same function must compile at every optimization level, so no pragmas are needed.

vector_width: for each line, drop everything after `#` or `;`, take the first word as the mnemonic, and test it against a regular expression for packed arithmetic: `v?(padd|psub|pmul)\w*` or `v?(add|sub|mul|div)p[sd]`. The widest register named in a matching line (xmm 128, ymm 256, zmm 512) is the answer, and 0 when nothing matches.
asm_variants and compile_variants use the same three settings: key "O0" is opt="-O0", key "O2" is opt="-O2", and key "O3_avx2" is opt="-O3" with flags=("-mavx2",).

sse2_add_asm: the arguments arrive in rdi (dst), rsi (a), rdx (b), and rcx (n, 64 bits). Keep an index i in rax. While i + 4 <= n, do movdqu xmm0, [rsi + rax*4]; movdqu xmm1, [rdx + rax*4]; paddd xmm0, xmm1; movdqu [rdi + rax*4], xmm0; and add 4 to i.

After the vector loop, a second loop handles the 0 to 3 leftover elements one at a time with 32-bit registers (`mov r8d, [rsi + rax*4]`, `add r8d, [rdx + rax*4]`). A length of 0 must skip both loops. Use movdqu, not movdqa: the arrays are not 16-byte aligned.

time_variants: for each library, call add_arrays on arrays of n elements `repeats` times, keep the smallest elapsed time from time.perf_counter(), and return it as seconds. Leave the "O3_avx2" entry out when cpu_has_avx2() is False.
